Platform: Customer Web + Provider Web + Admin Web
Scenario: Sessions expire in about 15 minutes with no silent refresh and die with the tab
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Sign in to any of the three apps 2) Leave the tab idle about 15 minutes 3) Navigate to any authenticated route
Expected Result: The session is refreshed transparently using the stored refresh token; the user stays signed in
Actual Result: All three apps bounce to the login screen. The JWT is held only in sessionStorage with no cookie; so the session is per-tab; a second tab is never signed in and closing the tab logs the user out
Recommended Fix: Refresh the access token in the background before expiry; move the session to a secure httpOnly cookie or a shared store so it survives tab changes

Expected Result: Payout should be the provider's actual earning - service value less platform commission - and must exclude tax collected on behalf of government and the platform fee
Actual Result: Both read ₹897.92; which is the full customer total including ₹63.92 tax and the ₹35 platform fee; while the service line itself is ₹799.00. No commission is deducted anywhere; so the figure promises the provider more than the business can pay and implies zero take rate

Scenario: JWT access token is passed in the WebSocket URL and logged to the console
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Sign in as provider 2) Open a job detail 3) Read the browser console
Expected Result: The token is sent via a header or a short-lived single-use ticket and never appears in a URL or the console
Actual Result: The console prints the full connection URL including access_token=<JWT> for both the tracking and chat hubs; tokens in query strings are recorded in proxy logs; server access logs and browser history; and here also in the console
Recommended Fix: Use SignalR access token negotiation that keeps the JWT out of the query string; or issue a short-lived single-use connection ticket; and stop logging connection URLs
column12: SignalR's own token mechanism; added configureLogging(Warning) to stop the client's default Information-level logging of the token-bearing URL. Token still rides the handshake query string only where SignalR's negotiate protocol requires it - a single-use ticket would need new backend infra
